title: QuietCare Home
short: A privacy-first smart home safety prototype for older adults, combining radar presence detection, wearable events and a caregiver dashboard.
description: QuietCare Home is a camera-free safety concept designed to help older adults live at home longer and more confidently. The prototype focuses on detecting possible falls, unusual inactivity and context events, while keeping the processing local-first and simple for caregivers.
problem: Existing emergency buttons only work when the resident remembers and is physically able to press them. Camera-based monitoring can feel too intrusive. QuietCare Home explores a middle ground: useful incident context without video monitoring.
solution: The concept combines a mmWave presence sensor, a wearable node and optional home sensors into a compact local hub. The dashboard shows clear states such as SAFE, MONITORING and ALERT, with acknowledgement and a demo workflow for testing.
impact: The goal is faster response, less privacy impact and better incident context for caregivers, housing organizations and families.
highlights: Sensor fusion between radar and wearable events
Caregiver workflow with alert, acknowledge and timeline
Designed for pilot testing in realistic home-care settings

title: Pit Analysis & Data Automation Tool
subtitle: Internship project focused on turning technical measurement data into readable insights.
short: During my software development internship at ASML, I worked on a data automation tool that helps convert technical pit measurement data into clearer, readable output. The project focused on improving the workflow from raw data to useful insights through a custom-built analysis interface.
summary: During my software development internship at ASML, I worked on a data automation tool that helps convert technical pit measurement data into clearer, readable output. The project focused on improving the workflow from raw data to useful insights through a custom-built analysis interface.
description: This internship project was focused on developing a Pit Analysis Tool for engineering-related data. The goal was to make complex measurement results easier to process, analyze and understand. Instead of manually reviewing raw data, the tool supports a more automated workflow where imported measurement files can be processed and visualized in a structured way. The project gave me hands-on experience with real-world software development, data handling, UI development and translating technical requirements into a working prototype.
problem: Technical measurement data can be difficult and time-consuming to review manually. The challenge was to create a clearer and more efficient workflow that helps users move from raw data to readable results.
solution: I developed a working application tool that imports measurement data, processes it into usable output and presents the results in a more understandable interface. The focus was on usability, structure, data automation and creating a solid foundation for future improvements.
impact: The tool provides a more efficient way to analyze pit measurement data, saving time and reducing the risk of errors. It also serves as a foundation for future enhancements, such as performance optimization, advanced analysis features and improved user experience.
highlights: Built a working application for pit data analysis
Created a more readable output from technical measurement data
Improved the workflow from raw files to structured results
Worked with real-world engineering data and software requirements
Gained experience with C#, WPF, .NET, data processing and MATLAB-based concepts
Explored future improvements such as performance, logging, UI refinement and advanced analysis features
responsibilities: Analyzed the problem and translated it into software requirements
Designed and developed the main prototype interface
Implemented data processing and result output functionality
Tested the tool with practical examples
Presented the project outcome and possible follow-up improvements
discreetNote: Project details have been simplified for portfolio use. Internal company information, sensitive datasets, specific workflows and confidential technical details are intentionally not included.
